pr.title: GVN: Allow reusing aggregates if LHS is not a simple local.
pr.description:
This resolves a FIXME in the code. I don't see a reason not to allow this.

pr.author: cjgillot

analysis.summary: GVN's aggregate-to-copy simplification was extended from only LHS locals to LHS places whose projections are all stable offsets. The safe optimization replaces a reconstructed aggregate with a copy from the value-numbered source aggregate, but it must not create an aliasing/overlapping assignment such as `*a = copy (*b)` when the LHS has a deref/non-stable projection, and its regression tests also guard against creating assignments between different fields of the same local.
analysis.originalLogic: In `simplify_aggregate_to_copy`, GVN first required a non-empty field list whose first value is `Value::Projection`, then required all fields to correspond one-to-one to the same aggregate and variant. If the source type matched `rvalue.ty(...)`, it called `self.try_as_place(copy_from_local_value, location, true)`; however, it only rewrote the rvalue to `Rvalue::Use(Operand::Copy(place))` when `lhs.as_local().is_some()`, and it returned `Some(copy_from_local_value)` even when it did not rewrite. The old FIXME said: "This also avoids any kind of projection, not just derefs. We can add allowed projections."
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The unsafe generalization would rewrite the aggregate to copy the source aggregate whenever the source type matches, even when the assignment target is a complex place containing a deref or other non-stable projection. That can produce `*a = copy (*b)`, where source and destination may alias and the assignment may overlap. The new code avoids this by computing `allow_complex_projection` as `lhs.projection[..].iter().all(PlaceElem::is_stable_offset)` and passing that to `try_as_place`. The `fields` regression test additionally keeps GVN from turning the aggregate assignment into a direct assignment between different fields of the same local, leaving the field extraction followed by `(_1.1: Adt) = Adt::Some(copy _2);`.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR after value numbering, where a place assignment's RHS is `Rvalue::Aggregate` and all aggregate fields are projections of one common source aggregate. The LHS may be a plain local or a projection that is either entirely stable offsets (e.g. `_1.0`) or contains a deref/complex projection (e.g. `*_4`). The source aggregate and the constructed aggregate must have the same type/variant.
analysis.trigger: GVN simplifies an aggregate: the field list is non-empty, the first field value is a `Value::Projection`, every field is a corresponding `ProjectionElem::Field` from the same aggregate value with matching indices, and `self.ty(copy_from_local_value) == ty`. If `try_as_place` returns a place, GVN rewrites the aggregate to `Rvalue::Use(Operand::Copy(place))` and records `self.reused_locals.insert(place.local)`. This rewrite is only safe when the LHS projection consists entirely of stable offsets.
preconditions: The aggregate has at least one field and its first field value is a `Value::Projection`.
All fields correspond one-to-one to fields of the same aggregate value, with matching variant/index.
The source aggregate type equals the aggregate being constructed: `self.ty(copy_from_local_value) == ty`.
A place can be produced by `try_as_place`; `allow_complex_projection` is `lhs.projection[..].iter().all(PlaceElem::is_stable_offset)`.
pitfalls: Allowing complex projections unconditionally can create `*a = copy (*b)`, where the two places may be aliases and the assignment overlaps.
Do not create assignments between different fields of the same local (guarded by the `fields` custom-MIR test).
The old code still returned `Some(value)` when it did not rewrite the rvalue; do not conflate "aggregate recognized as copyable" with "rvalue was actually rewritten".
Borrowing restrictions and post-copy overwrites are separate conditions; do not conflate them with the aliasing/overlap check on the LHS projection.
The type check changed from `rvalue.ty(...)` to the explicit aggregate `ty`; both sides must be the same type/variant.
analysis.testStrategy: Use custom MIR with `// EMIT_MIR gvn_overlapping.<case>.GVN.diff` and CHECK/CHECK-NEXT assertions on the before/after MIR. Add `stable_projection` so a stable LHS projection `_1.0` with a deref RHS `*_4` is optimized from `(_1.0: Adt) = Adt::Some(copy _3);` to `(_1.0: Adt) = copy (*_4);`. Add `fields` so `_1.1 = Adt::Some(_2)` is not replaced by an assignment from a different field of `_1`, retaining `_2 = copy (((_1.0: Adt) as variant#1).0: u32);` then `(_1.1: Adt) = Adt::Some(copy _2);`. Add an overlapping case using a deref LHS projection and verify no overlapping copy assignment is introduced.
evidence: GVN: Allow reusing aggregates if LHS is not a simple local.
This resolves a FIXME in the code. I don't see a reason not to allow this.
